who.value: seller listing Pokemon TCG cards, casual to regular

job.value: Upload a photo, paste a link, or live-scan multiple cards so AI extracts the card's attributes

arrivedFrom.value: Sell button, choosing a TCG card scan entry

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: 'TCG Scanner' title, the 'Choose photo' drop zone and 'Ready to scan' make clear the screen scans a card from a photo.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The large dashed 'Choose photo' area is the obvious first step, but the 'Scan card' button is a disabled grey bar that reads weaker than the empty-state illustration below it.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Upload photo', 'Scan multiple', 'Image link', 'Choose photo – Camera or photo library' and 'Scan card' each say what they do.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'TCG' in the title is fine for this audience, but 'Image link' / 'paste a direct image link' assumes the seller knows what a direct image URL is.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: Picking a photo is easy, but the three tabs ask the seller to choose an input method before scanning even though the body says 'We'll detect single or multiple cards automatically'.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Only the upload zone and a short empty state are shown; scan results and card details are deferred until a photo is chosen.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Everything — tabs, upload zone, 'Scan card' — is about getting a card into the listing flow.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: The upload zone carries itself, but the 'Ready to scan' block repeats the instruction in a 3-line paragraph below the button that adds little.
